statement: color palette: Nearly every AI-built page changes the overall palette, most often to a navy/blue family, with teal/green, warm cream with orange or rust accents, and dark near-black schemes as the other common outcomes, and only o

text and link colors: AI-built pages commonly standardise text and links, most often turning mid-grey or near-black body text into a darker, cooler tone with grey secondary copy, and making links underlined or recolored.

section backgrounds: Most AI-built pages break the page into alternating full-width section bands, typically white or cream alternating with pale tints or dark navy/slate bands, replacing plain white or the original's differing ba

accent color: Most AI-built pages swap the original's accent hue for a different, usually more muted or deeper one (burnt orange, teal, indigo, gold), with a few reassigning or consolidating the accent role.
page background: Page backgrounds mostly shift to off-white or white from darker or saturated grounds, while a couple keep the original background.

footer: Nearly every footer is rebuilt, most commonly into a dark (navy, near-black or green) footer that is either a three- or four-column link layout or a slim single band, with a few legal-text footers kept as they were.

buttons and calls to action: Buttons and calls to action were changed on nearly every site, most often into rounded pill buttons in a new color, commonly as a filled and outline pair, and sometimes from text links into solid butto

primary navigation: Primary navigation is almost always rebuilt as a simple single-row set of plain text links inside the header, typically right-aligned (sometimes translucent/blurred or on a solid bar), with only a few left unch
social links: Social icons are most often replaced by plain text links or text pill buttons, with some restyled as circular badges and a few dropped entirely.
product cards: Product and brand cards are commonly rebuilt as bordered, uniform or equal-height cards, often swapping images for text, with a few kept and a few added.
newsletter signup: Newsletter signups are commonly lifted out of the footer into a centered full-width band or card with a single email field and pill-style button.
search control: Search controls are mostly restyled into a plain input with a square or labeled button, or moved/repurposed elsewhere, and two header searches are dropped.
content section layout: Content sections were usually rebuilt into more structured layouts such as columns, cards, bands or accordions, and a few were kept or newly added.
navigation menu controls: Navigation controls were generally simplified, with recolored active items, redrawn carets and menu toggles, and hidden mega-menus and drawers dropped.
forms and inputs: Forms were either restyled with clearer labels and real buttons or, when hidden or secondary, dropped, and only a few were kept as they were.
about section: Most AI-built about sections are rebuilt as a two-column layout pairing text with a photo, stats or card, with a few instead restyled as a paragraph, band or background.
blog post feed: Blog feeds are most often rebuilt as uniform card grids, frequently text-only and bordered, with some content dropped and a few added placeholder or orphan tiles.
category tiles: Category and link tiles are mostly converted into white or neutral bordered cards, sometimes with added fixed-height or uneven-row artifacts.
promo cards, callouts and badges: Promo strips, notices and ribbons were typically recast as cards, bands or pill badges in the new palette, with a few dropped or kept.
announcement bar: Announcement bars are most often restyled into thin solid-color strips or cards, while a couple are dropped and one is kept unchanged.
header: All observed headers become a slimmer solid bar, usually white or dark, with a smaller logo and simple links.
sidebar widgets: Sidebar widgets are mostly pulled out of the sidebar into full-width sections, grids or footer text, with occasional restyling or dropping.
news list: News lists are usually recast as bordered or hairline-ruled entry lists, with a couple becoming card grids and one kept.
utility bar: Utility bars are usually rebuilt as a thin dark navy or green bar carrying links, search or contact details.
feature section: One-off feature sections with photos are generally reworked into two-column or card layouts instead of full-bleed photo bands.
section action links: Section action links are converted either into right-aligned underlined text links or into outlined pill buttons, with one kept as is.
content cards: Content blocks are turned into uniform bordered white card grids, usually three columns and often text-only.
link list: Plain text link lists are typically restyled with new link colors, hairline rules or bordered rows and tiles.
logo band: Logo bands are typically converted from bare logo rows into white or bordered tiles on a tinted band, occasionally producing tile artifacts, and one is dropped.
site statistics: Statistics are typically presented as separate stat cards, tiles or hero-area blocks rather than the original's inline or oversized-number formats.
promo cards: Promo imagery is reworked into image-top, text-below or bordered cards laid out in a row, replacing overlays, sliders and banners.
quick links: Quick links are generally converted into bordered text cards or button grids, replacing icon tiles, overlays or sidebar menus.
header utilities and misc widgets: Small utility elements were mostly dropped or redrawn as pills and text links, and third-party badges and broken plugin blocks did not carry over.
contact section: Contact information is pulled out of footers or widgets into its own structured section, often two-column or built as a definition list.
hero carousel: The rotating hero sliders were generally simplified, with several reduced to a single slide with indicator dots or lost their pagination.
suggested searches: Suggested searches appear as rounded chips, either newly added keyword pills or converted from a text link line.
value pillars: Value propositions are mostly laid out as three-column card or icon rows on a colored band.
video module: Video modules were usually restructured or restyled into different containers or placeholders, with one site dropping the empty embed entirely.
post category labels: Category bars are usually reduced to small uppercase colored kicker labels, with one label dropped.
instagram feed: Instagram feeds are rebuilt as grids of tiles, mostly text-only where the original images were broken.
events section: Events areas were split between being kept nearly as-is and being enlarged into a centered block or card.
timestamps: Timestamps were mostly converted to or kept as long-form dates in time elements, with one site dropping relative timestamps.
districts presentation: Districts are turned from icon lists or map panels into outlined tiles or pill chips.
sponsor block: Sponsor blocks are simplified into flatter cards or labeled ads.
empty-carousel content sections: Carousel areas that rendered blank in the originals were typically replaced with visible static columns, cards or figures, usually three of them.
careers link: A careers entry was promoted from a plain footer link to its own section with a paragraph or button.
login form: Login forms were either surfaced as a visible hero card or newly added with social sign-in next to contact content, so the form became more prominent in both cases.
copy tone: Copy tone was either kept close to the original or flattened into short, plain, sentence-case, non-exclamatory and often third-person text, with no emoji or em dashes.
footer legal text: Footer legal text was kept as a copyright line on about half the sites, while the rest shortened, rewrote or restyled it into a small line.
link affordance: Link affordances were commonly changed to use trailing arrows, often text arrows on underlined links or on read more links.
content and dates: The AI-built pages almost always keep the original's content items, dates, repeated posts, registration details and labels unchanged.
post meta line: Post meta lines were restyled or reformatted on each of the five sites, usually into smaller, quieter bylines, eyebrows or date labels, with no single common pattern.
section subtitles: On all five sites the AI-built pages have a muted subtitle paragraph under section headings (mostly h2, once h1), usually newly added.
contact details: Contact details were most often restructured, either into labelled definition lists with email links or repeated across header, footer and other places, and in one case dropped.
repeated calls to action: Repeated calls to action were either kept as in the original (two of four sites) or altered, simplified or dropped on the others.
corner radius: Most AI-built pages change the original's square corners to small rounding (often with pill shapes on buttons or tags), while a few go to larger radii and only two keep square corners.

visual effects: The AI-built pages mostly reduce effects, with many original transitions cut back or removed and shadows or gradients swapped for flat styling and thin borders, though about a quarter keep an already minimal effect
section dividers: Original thick, dotted, torn-edge or banded dividers were commonly dropped or reduced to hairline rules and spacing, with a couple of sites adding hairline rules where none existed.
card accent border: On the few sites with this feature, cards gained or altered a border treatment, typically a category-coded colored left border or a thin grey outline.

image treatment: Photos are commonly normalized into uniform, rounded or framed crops, with broken or missing images replaced by flat placeholders or dropped and many-image layouts reduced to a few images, though a fair number of
logo: Logos are most often shrunk or turned into styled text wordmarks, with a minority kept as the original image and a few repositioned.
icons: Across many sites, icon fonts and inline SVG icons are replaced by emoji, text glyphs or raster images, or dropped, while some raster icons are kept as they were.
section and banner images: These one-off banner, illustration and decorative images are mostly repositioned or resized into their own sections, with a few added or dropped.
payment logos: Payment logos are mostly re-laid out into horizontal rows or centered sections, with single cases of being kept, added or dropped.
product images: Where product images were broken or missing, the AI pages typically substitute labeled placeholders or cards rather than real photos.
certification badge: Certification badges are split between being kept as raster images and being moved or enlarged.
avatars: On all three sites where avatars appear, the AI-built page renders them as circles.
image text overlay: Text over images is handled differently on each site, with baked-in text kept, converted to live HTML, or overlay headlines removed.
page layout: Most AI-built pages move to a flex-plus-grid layout, replacing floats, flexbox-only or tables, and many collapse sidebar layouts into single-column or stacked full-width sections.

hero area: The most common outcome is that full-bleed photo or slider heroes are rebuilt as two-column text-and-image heroes, often with gradient or tinted backgrounds, while a few banners are kept and others become overlay or tex
content column width: Most AI-built pages place content in a centered column of about 1040–1120px, often with full-bleed bands, whatever the original width or alignment.
page length: Page height changes on most sites, most often with a very tall page becoming much shorter, while a smaller group becomes taller and a few lose empty gaps above the footer.

spacing rhythm: Spacing is usually made more regular, with large gaps, inconsistent indents or crowding replaced or supplemented by consistent gutters and section padding, while a few sites keep their generous whitespace.
text alignment and column width: In these few cases, text blocks are re-aligned, most often from centered to left-aligned columns or sections, with isolated changes to intro, hero and wrapped text.
footer link columns: Footer link columns are handled differently in each of the few sites, being dropped, turned into cards or accordions, or given uneven column heights.
gallery grid: Gallery grids are reworked into wrapping grids or shorter rows, or dropped, with no single pattern across the three sites.
body typeface: Body typefaces were replaced on every site, most commonly with a system-ui stack and otherwise with Georgia plus a sans pairing or a Helvetica stack.
body text size and line height: Body text was almost always normalized to 16–17px with a 1.6–1.65 line height regardless of the original size or spacing.
h1 heading: The h1 was usually changed, most often from an absent, empty, hidden or small heading into a large, bold, visible h1 (frequently white or navy, sentence case, sometimes serif).

section headings: Section headings were changed on nearly every site, typically toward bolder, navy-colored or size-contrasted h2s, with some becoming left-aligned or live text and some gaining underline bars.
section eyebrow labels: AI-built pages most often added uppercase letterspaced eyebrow labels above section headings, while handwritten script eyebrows were kept on one site and dropped on another.

letterspaced uppercase text: Letterspaced uppercase text was commonly altered, with all-caps headings, buttons and nav converted to sentence case while wide-tracked uppercase was kept only for eyebrow labels.
card text hierarchy: Card text hierarchies were mostly restyled in small, site-specific ways (e.g., new title, date, excerpt or label styling), with only a couple kept as in the original.
post titles: Post titles were handled differently on each of the few sites, with truncation dropped or kept and one restyle into sentence-case serif h3s.
inline emphasis: A couple of AI-built pages added colored or bold inline emphasis on key terms or a heading phrase.
